articleMarkdown:
# Studying Jiā Rén (The Family): close relationships also need clear responsibilities

When living together, make needs, responsibilities, and boundaries explicit so that care becomes dependable daily practice.

The closer we are, the easier it is to assume that others should know our needs. Jiā Rén discusses order in shared life, while explicitly retaining ancient ideas of men outside, women inside, and stern household authority. Studying it means neither erasing these historical limitations nor turning them into present-day rules about who must do housework or obey.

## Identity and line order

Jiā Rén is hexagram 37 in the traditional King Wen sequence, with symbol ䷤. The lower trigram is Lí ☲ and the upper trigram is Xùn ☴; their traditional images are fire and wind, respectively. Count the lines from the bottom: 初九、六二、九三、六四、九五、上九. A solid line is yang and a broken line is yin. Nine and six in the line labels designate yang and yin; they are not additional line numbers.

```text
━━━━━━━━━  上九
━━━━━━━━━  九五
━━━━ ━━━━  六四
━━━━━━━━━  九三
━━━━ ━━━━  六二
━━━━━━━━━  初九
```

## Hexagram statement

家人：利女貞。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: The family: the woman's steadfast correctness is beneficial.

Within an ancient household structure, Legge reads this as a wife's appropriate steadfastness benefiting domestic affairs. That is the selected historical translator's understanding, not a requirement that modern households divide work by gender.

Today, a broader question is which ongoing labor and commitments sustain shared life, who performs them, and whose needs remain unseen. Those involved should discuss responsibilities according to circumstances and willingness; a hexagram does not assign their roles.

References: [zhouyi-37](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/家人&oldid=2405005), [legge1882-37](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Interpretations in the Ten Wings

The Commentary on the Judgment and the Commentary on the Images belong to the commentarial collection known as the Yìzhuàn, usually called the Ten Wings. Below, these commentaries are kept separate from the hexagram and line statements, followed by modern learning applications.

The Commentary on the Judgment explicitly discusses the ordering of family roles. The Commentary on the Images takes wind emerging from fire and calls for substance in words and constancy in conduct. The latter can help us notice whether language is specific and actions reliable.

Saying which task you will take on is clearer than simply saying you will help. Reliability also includes communicating promptly when conditions change. Affection within a household must not become an unlimited obligation requiring no explanation.

References: [zhouyi-37](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/家人&oldid=2405005), [hon-sep](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/chinese-change/)

## The six lines, from bottom to top

### 初九 · Explain shared agreements from the beginning

閑有家，悔亡。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Set boundaries for the household; regret disappears.

Xián here concerns safeguards and boundaries; Legge reads the first line as establishing household rules. Stricter is not necessarily better: rules also need justification and intelligibility.

When beginning to live together, discuss shared space, expenses, and daily arrangements. Everyone should have a chance to speak, rather than letting the most forceful person simply announce the rules.

References: [zhouyi-37](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/家人&oldid=2405005), [legge1882-37](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 六二 · Recognize the labor that sustains daily life

无攸遂，在中饋，貞吉。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Pursuing no separate course, attending to food within the household: steadfast correctness brings good fortune.

The household food provision is the focus of zhōng kuì, which Legge interprets within the wife's traditional role. It brings otherwise inconspicuous everyday work into the text.

Modern readers can value that labor without assigning it to one gender. Cooking, cleaning, and care take real time and should be recognized and fairly shared.

References: [zhouyi-37](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/家人&oldid=2405005), [legge1882-37](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九三 · Rules and respect both need to be present

家人嗃嗃，悔厲吉；婦子嘻嘻，終吝。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: The household is stern: regret and danger, yet good fortune. Women and children laughing carelessly: regret in the end.

The ancient text evaluates sternness and laughter differently, and Legge's interpretation also favors strict governance. That historical view cannot justify humiliating, frightening, or harming family members.

Today, combine clear requests with considerate expression. Problems require attention and people retain their dignity. Claiming that everything is for someone's own good cannot cancel disagreement.

References: [zhouyi-37](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/家人&oldid=2405005), [legge1882-37](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 六四 · A flourishing shared life does not belong to one person

富家，大吉。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Enriching the household: great good fortune.

Legge reads this as bringing abundance to the household, still emphasizing the wife's role within his traditional division of labor. This article does not treat it as a forecast of future income.

Today, ask how existing resources can meet shared needs. Control over resources does not confer unlimited power to decide for every member.

References: [zhouyi-37](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/家人&oldid=2405005), [legge1882-37](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 九五 · Public responsibility also appears in daily life

王假有家，勿恤，吉。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: The king comes to his household. Do not worry; good fortune.

The king is linked with the household; Legge reads this as influence extending into the home. The text is not a reason for a modern family to require a king.

The values someone expresses publicly should also be tested against daily conduct. Respect and responsibility need to appear in small actions, not only in attractive public statements.

References: [zhouyi-37](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/家人&oldid=2405005), [legge1882-37](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

### 上九 · Reliability and boundaries are not built on fear

有孚威如，終吉。

Original editorial rendering; not a quotation from Legge: Sincerity with dignified authority: good fortune in the end.

Sincerity and authority appear together. Legge emphasizes honesty, self-cultivation, and appropriate dignity; the Commentary on the Images also speaks of turning back to examine oneself.

Begin by requiring yourself to keep agreements, then discuss responsibilities with others. Clear boundaries matter, but authority must not mean making people afraid, forbidding objections, or demanding obedience.

References: [zhouyi-37](https://zh.wikisource.org/w/index.php?title=周易/家人&oldid=2405005), [legge1882-37](https://tianmu.org/good-work-library/confucian/general-texts/the-i-ching-james-legge)

## Reconsidering the division of work in a shared home

Original modern scenario

Two people living together often resent the state of shared areas. One feels they always do the work; the other assumes that greater concern means a willingness to handle everything. They first list the actual tasks instead of reducing the disagreement to who cares less.

They redistribute work according to time and ability, explain what completion means, and agree to revise an arrangement that does not fit. Neither gender nor personality makes anyone permanently responsible for the same task.

The modern value of Jiā Rén is turning care into concrete action, rather than treating closeness as permission for every demand.

## Misreadings to avoid

- Ancient gender roles and patriarchal authority must remain in historical context. This article supports no household control, humiliation, or violence.

- Jiā Rén does not decide who should marry, have children, or take a particular role, nor establish that family relationships will necessarily go smoothly.

## Three practices

1. List one often-overlooked task that sustains shared life.

2. Rewrite a vague expectation as a specific request that can be discussed.

3. Check whether current agreements preserve respect, privacy, and reasonable boundaries for everyone.

## Related hexagram

### Kuí — Opposition (hexagram-38)

Jiā Rén concerns how shared life works; Kuí helps address differences that remain within close relationships. Closeness does not require identical views, needs, or ways of expressing oneself.

## A closing question

While reading Jiā Rén, ask: has what we call care become a daily practice that each of us can understand and undertake?
